turns.assessment: The failure is localized to the launch of OMS S19->S06. Every amplifier on that OMS lost input and output power, including booster amp0, while pump currents remained unchanged and monitored incoming signals at S19 showed no change. This rules strongly against an amplifier or downstream span failure and, with recent maintenance at S19, points to a disconnected/broken input patch between the S19 ROADM degree and booster.

proposals.rationale: The booster itself lost input power and all downstream stages and channels lost signal, while amplifier pump currents and incoming optical signals at S19 remained normal. A pulled OMS input patch at S19 exactly produces this all-channel hard loss; recent S19 maintenance increases its likelihood.

A hard ROADM port failure at S19 could block channels without disturbing incoming line monitoring, but failure of one WSS input port is less consistent with loss of every channel launched onto S19->S06 than the common output patch being disconnected.
The same patch is correctly localized, but contamination normally causes reduced power rather than complete simultaneous loss at the booster input.
